This 
document outlines 
the checklist 
I1 for Rosemount pressure 
transmitter (Flow Transmitter) 0-1250 mm H2O, 24 
Vdc, 
 4 - 20 ma, 
which must be carried out on 
an annually bases as indicated 
by Y1 in the above title block.

The first draft initiated by eng.
 Ahmed Esmail Fouad and eng. Khalil Awad, 
 and internet assistance by eng. Mohamed Selim Salman conducting with 
 MPIS office at EEHC, the document field tested at 1 
 Dec.2002 and 
 revised by quality control eng. Abdel Menem Al Emam at EDEPCo., accepted by 
 general director: eng Mohamed Abdel Ghafar, and approved by eng. Awad Fathy 
 Head Sector of EL-Aresh Power Station.

items:
A work order 
 must be issued, the maintenance staff should be qualified and carry the 
 suitable safety category.

Safety fence with caution marks 
 surrrounding the work area is required.

Wear safety 
 helmet, shoes.

Close manual 
 valves for Transmitter lines.
Safety helmet, shoes,
Digital Ammeter.
Pressure tester.

Adjustable 
 open end Spanner.
Review technical reference material and manufactures manual.
Obtain copy of Indicator field maintenance file.
Remove transmitter indicator and connect the ammeter leads.

Open high vent 
 to atmosphere and connect the pressure tester to high vent of transmitter

Record the ammeter 
 reading for 0 mm H2O.

Using 
 pressure tester inject 1250 mm H2O and record the ammeter reading.

Vent out the 
 pressure and record the ammeter reading.

Compare the 
 ammeter reading with the field maintenance file if there is any error repeat 
 step 3 to adjust Zero and step 4 to adjust Span .

Repeat steps 
 3,4, and 5 until reach the required ammeter reading.

Return transmitter to service by removing the ammeter leads from the indicator 
 terminal and connect the indicator.
Remove the pressure tester .
Open the manual valves for transmitter lines.
Vent out air from transmitter lines.
Close low and high vents.

Place a copy of 
 test result in the field maintenance file.

text:
Power 
 Stations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This 
document outlines 
the checklist 
I1 for Rosemount pressure 
transmitter (Flow Transmitter) 0-1250 mm H2O, 24 
Vdc, 
 4 - 20 ma, 
which must be carried out on 
an annually bases as indicated 
by Y1 in the above title block.
The first draft initiated by eng.
 Ahmed Esmail Fouad and eng. Khalil Awad, 
 and internet assistance by eng. Mohamed Selim Salman conducting with 
 MPIS office at EEHC, the document field tested at 1 
 Dec.2002 and 
 revised by quality control eng. Abdel Menem Al Emam at EDEPCo., accepted by 
 general director: eng Mohamed Abdel Ghafar, and approved by eng. Awad Fathy 
 Head Sector of EL-Aresh Power Station.
Safety 
Precautions
A work order 
 must be issued, the maintenance staff should be qualified and carry the 
 suitable safety category.
Safety fence with caution marks 
 surrrounding the work area is required.
Wear safety 
 helmet, shoes.
Close manual 
 valves for Transmitter lines.
Tools and Equipments
Safety helmet, shoes,
Digital Ammeter.
Pressure tester.
Adjustable 
 open end Spanner.
Work to be carried out
Steps to Prepare for test
Review technical reference material and manufactures manual.
Obtain copy of Indicator field maintenance file.
Remove transmitter indicator and connect the ammeter leads.
Open high vent 
 to atmosphere and connect the pressure tester to high vent of transmitter
Testing Procedure
Record the ammeter 
 reading for 0 mm H2O.
Using 
 pressure tester inject 1250 mm H2O and record the ammeter reading.
Vent out the 
 pressure and record the ammeter reading.
Inject 25% 
 (312.5 mm H2O ) , 50% ( 625 mmH2O), 75% ( 937.5 mmH2O) and 100% (1250 mmH2O).
Compare the 
 ammeter reading with the field maintenance file if there is any error repeat 
 step 3 to adjust Zero and step 4 to adjust Span .
Repeat steps 
 3,4, and 5 until reach the required ammeter reading.
Return Transmitter to 
Service
Return transmitter to service by removing the ammeter leads from the indicator 
 terminal and connect the indicator.
Remove the pressure tester .
Open the manual valves for transmitter lines.
Vent out air from transmitter lines.
Close low and high vents.
Place a copy of 
 test result in the field maintenance file.
